e-12524.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/7444a8128c085d7bf4f56a57a60c260864a50da0b744b6dbe22a2ced89a0588d.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/22dd960829ea268e5aade685b56949f8998f87ae8c040a90f04436cbfc6b9a58.png)

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/4fede2bb5c2306f62b55b7996488baee52c69e7d41b011e0e9d2b7405e63a8f4.png)

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})={x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $\left(1,0\right).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{x}^{2})=1-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2xy)=1-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{x}^{2})=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & 1-2x \\ 1-2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,2).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1,2)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[y−2xyx−x2], we must have

∂f∂x=y−2xy,∂f∂y=x−x2.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(y−2xy)=−2y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x−x2)=1−2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(y−2xy)=1−2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x−x2)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[−2y1−2x1−2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (1,2). This gives

f″(1,2)=[−4−1−10].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-2xy & x-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y-2xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x-{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2xy)=-2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{x}^{2})=1-2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2xy)=1-2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{x}^{2})=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-2y & 1-2x \\ 1-2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(1,2).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1,2)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=10xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=5{x}^{2}-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy)=10y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=10x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy)=10x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[10xy5x2−2y], we must have

∂f∂x=10xy,∂f∂y=5x2−2y.

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(10xy)=10y∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(5x2−2y)=10x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(10xy)=10x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(5x2−2y)=−2

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[10y10x10x−2].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (12,12). This gives

f″(12,12)=[555−2].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}10xy & 5{x}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=10xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=5{x}^{2}-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy)=10y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=10x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy)=10x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5{x}^{2}-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}10y & 10x \\ 10x & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=e-{e}^{2-x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(e-{e}^{2-x})={e}^{2-x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)=0 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e-{e}^{2-x})=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)=2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}e-{e}^{2-x} & 2y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=e-{e}^{2-x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(e-{e}^{2-x})={e}^{2-x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)=0 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e-{e}^{2-x})=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)=2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2-x} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:

${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-4y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}-4x-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4y+1)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y+1)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=6y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -4 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}-4y+1 & 3{y}^{2}-4x-1\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-4y+1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}-4x-1.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4y+1)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4y+1)=-4\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-4x-1)=6y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -4 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]$
after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y & 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(2,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[2xsin⁡yx2cos⁡y], we must have

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function Given Its First Derivative
content.problem:
Find ${f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}]$
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y & {x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y & 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y & -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(2,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(2,\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x(y-1) & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(y-1))=2(y-1)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1)=2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(y-1))=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2(y-1) & 2x \\ 2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x((y−1)(x2−1))∂∂y((y−1)(x2−1))]=[2x(y−1)x2−1]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(2x(y−1))=2(y−1)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(x2−1)=2x∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(2x(y−1))=2x∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(x2−1)=0

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[2(y−1)2x2x0].

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at (−1,2). This gives

f″(−1,2)=[2−2−20].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1)) & \frac{∂}{∂y}((y-1)({x}^{2}-1))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x(y-1) & {x}^{2}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(y-1))=2(y-1)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1)=2x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(y-1))=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2(y-1) & 2x \\ 2x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn),

the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix

f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

In our case, we have

f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, we compute the first derivative of f(x,y), as follows:

f′(x,y)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]=[∂∂x(xsin⁡y+xy)∂∂y(xsin⁡y+xy)]=[sin⁡y+yxcos⁡y+x]

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(sin⁡y+y)=0∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(xcos⁡y+x)=cos⁡y+1∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(sin⁡y+y)=cos⁡y+1∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(xcos⁡y+x)=−xsin⁡y

So, the second derivative is

f″(x,y)=[0cos⁡y+1cos⁡y+1−xsin⁡y].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Function
content.worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y & x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+x)=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y+1 & -x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
